radiology_report:
LUMC (Leiden)
Imaging Department
Date: 22 November 2024
Exam: mpMRI Prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 82.0 ng/mL, prior biopsy Gleason 4+4, PI-RADS 5
FINDINGS: Prostate volume measures 64.0 mL. A dominant lesion is identified in the left peripheral zone at the apex, measuring approximately 18 x 15 x 12 mm. The lesion demonstrates marked restricted diffusion on DWI (b=1400) with corresponding early and intense enhancement on DCE. T2-weighted imaging shows a focal area of low signal intensity replacing the normal peripheral zone architecture. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone apex. PSA density 1.281 ng/mL/mL. Clinical T stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.9339169.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 9.0 ng/mL. After discussion, a referral to urology was initiated for further evaluation and potential biopsy. Blood pressure and lipid levels were reviewed, and current medications were deemed stable.

previous_notes.author: Dr. H. Martens (GP)
previous_notes.text: PSA repeated at 5.8 ng/mL, showing a decrease from previous measurement. Patient reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms, currently managed with tamsulosin. Referred for urological assessment to discuss persistent concern despite fluctuating PSA levels.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1: The histological examination reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 4+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone at the left apex. A cribriform pattern is present. Perineural invasion is identified.

Summary: The pathological trajectory shows a persistent high-grade disease profile with no change in the reported Gleason score or ISUP grade group across the available timepoints.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
